_meta.note: Informational only. Maps a detected library + exact version against publicly disclosed CVEs so a researcher can prioritize manual verification. This file contains no exploit code or PoCs, only public advisory references.
_meta.rangeSyntax: Ranges use simple comparators: '<x.y.z', '<=x.y.z', '>=x.y.z <a.b.c'. Comparison is numeric, dot-separated.

entries.summary: Untrusted HTML passed to jQuery's DOM manipulation methods (e.g. .html()) can execute injected <script> elements — XSS.
Similar untrusted-HTML XSS vector affecting jQuery(<>) and related methods prior to the 3.5.0 sanitization fix.
jQuery.extend(true, ...) prototype pollution allowing property injection into Object.prototype.
Command injection via the template function when a malicious template string reaches it (also related prototype pollution history in earlier 4.x versions).
Prototype pollution in defaultsDeep() allowing an attacker to modify Object.prototype.
Prototype pollution via zipObjectDeep() (and related pick/set/update family) when property paths are attacker-controlled, letting an attacker inject properties onto Object.prototype.
XSS via the Datepicker widget's altField option when populated with untrusted input.
XSS via other Datepicker widget text options (e.g. button/display strings) when populated with untrusted input.
XSS via the of option of the .position() utility when given an attacker-influenced selector string.
ReDoS (catastrophic backtracking) in moment's string-to-date parsing when given crafted input.
XSS in the tooltip/popover data-template attribute due to insufficient sanitization.
Same tooltip/popover XSS vector, patched across the 3.x and 4.x lines at these versions.
Leaks the XSRF-TOKEN cookie value in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on every request when withCredentials is enabled, including to unrelated cross-origin hosts.
